parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing positives dominate the everyday exposure: no presentation offence, no facility or border restriction documented, gender-identity discrimination prohibited since 2012, hate-speech law, marriage equality, and active LGBT community infrastructure. No island-specific violence or enforcement record exists — moderately positive given functioning national institutions, but not proof of safety. The clear negative is custody: placement follows document gender marker, most trans women end up in all-male facilities facing threats, and the 2021 watchdog found persistent serious violations across all establishments since 2010 — an unremedied institutional exposure (tier 1-2) corroborated by oversight findings. But this is conditional on detention, not a universal exposure reaching every visitor, and its evidentiary base is national rather than island-specific. Net: acceptance plus working legal protections with a serious but non-inevitable custody exposure sits above 0.65, below 0.75.
